newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PONTING LIFTS TASMANIA WITH ANOTHER CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PONTING LIFTS TASMANIA WITH ANOTHER CENTURY.

text.p: Discarded Australia test batsman Ricky Ponting scored his third consecutive first-class century to give Tasmania the upper hand in their Sheffield Shield match against Queensland on Friday.
Tasmania reached a commanding 305 for six at Bellerive Oval in Hobart at close of play on the first day against Queensland, one of their rivals for a place in the Sheffield Shield final.
Ponting, overlooked for Australia's current tour of South Africa, enhanced his claim for a recall for the test series in England later this year with a superb 159, including 20 fours, off 263 balls.

Shield leaders Western Australia badly dented New South Wales' prospects of reaching the final, contested by the top two teams in the standings at the end of the regular season, by routing the visitors for 89 at the WACA Ground in Perth.
Off-spinner Bret Mulder claimed five wickets at a cost of two runs in a dramatic six-over spell as New South Wales lost their last seven first innings wickets for the addition of just four runs.
At the end of the first day, Western Australian were 211 for seven, with wicketkeeper Adam Gilchrist unbeaten on 65.
In Adelaide, visitors Victoria dominated the first day by dismissing South Australia for 216 before reaching a comfortable 72 for one at close of play.
With an outright win worth six points, Western Australia head the Shield table with 30 points, six clear of Tasmania. Queensland and New South Wales are locked together on 22 points.
